subject: System Integration & Architecture
title: Summative Exam: System Integration, SOA, REST APIs & Middleware

questions.text: Which integration method connects every sub-system directly to every other sub-system, resulting in a complex web of connections often called 'Spaghetti Integration'?
What is the primary advantage of using an Enterprise Service Bus (ESB) for integration?
options: It eliminates the need for data transformation
It creates a direct connection between every pair of systems
It allows each system to connect to a central hub, reducing the number of required connections
It is the fastest integration method for small-scale systems

questions.text: Which of the following is an international standard for electronic data interchange across administration, commerce, and transport sectors?
Which SOA principle ensures that changes inside one service do not break connected systems as long as the interface remains unchanged?
In a Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA), what is the role of a Service Registry?
options: To allow service providers to publish services and consumers to discover them

questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of a Microservices architecture?
options: Single large codebase with all business logic
Centralized database shared by all services
Independently deployable services with their own databases

questions.text: What does REST stand for in the context of web APIs?
Which HTTP method is used in RESTful APIs to completely replace an existing resource?
In REST architecture, what is a representation of a resource?
options: The actual data stored in the database
The state of a resource including data, metadata, and hypermedia links

questions.text: Which REST constraint requires that the server stores no session data between requests?
Which messaging pattern allows a single message to be delivered to multiple consumers simultaneously?
What is the primary advantage of asynchronous messaging over synchronous RPC?
options: It provides immediate feedback to the user
It decouples the producer from the consumer, improving fault tolerance

questions.text: Which integration pattern is commonly used for scheduled bulk data migration into data warehouses?
Which type of middleware provides a centralized hub for routing, transforming, and mediating messages between disparate systems?
In the Software Testing Pyramid, which type of testing occupies the widest base and should have the most test cases?
What is the primary goal of System Integration Testing (SIT)?
options: To test individual functions in isolation
To verify that distinct modules and services interact correctly as a unified system
To validate end-to-end user workflows against business requirements
To measure system performance under load

questions.text: Which type of testing ensures that new features or updates do not break existing integrations?
Which deployment strategy uses two identical environments and switches live traffic instantly, allowing zero downtime and immediate rollback?
What is a key benefit of Canary Deployment?
options: It minimizes the blast radius by exposing only a small percentage of users to a new release
It automatically rolls back all changes

questions.text: In a CI/CD pipeline, what is the primary function of Continuous Integration (CI)?
options: To deploy code directly to production
To automatically merge code changes and trigger builds and tests

questions.text: According to ISO 9241-11, usability is defined by three core components. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
In usability testing, what is the difference between a 'slip' and a 'mistake'?
options: A slip is a system error; a mistake is a user error
A slip is a physical error with the right goal; a mistake is having the wrong goal
A slip is a minor error; a mistake is a critical error
There is no difference; they are synonyms

questions.text: What is the System Usability Scale (SUS)?
options: A 10-question survey producing a score from 0 to 100
A programming framework for building APIs

questions.text: All APIs are web services, but not all web services are APIs.
RESTful APIs require data to be formatted exclusively in XML.
Message-Oriented Middleware (MOM) allows applications to communicate synchronously, where the sender waits for a response before continuing.
The formula N(N-1)/2 calculates the number of connections required in which integration method?
The architectural style where software is designed as a collection of discrete, loosely coupled, and reusable services is known as _______.
The messaging pattern where only one consumer processes each message from a queue is called _______.
The process of continuously merging code changes into a central repository to trigger automated builds and tests is known as _______.
